svg.title: It is a real overlap in a calibrated relative-phase convention, not an absolute fidelity: |⟨v0, v1⟩| = 1 alone permits an unknown relative phase of π and cannot protect this reader. The certificate is a physical premise or an independently justified calibration result. Reading all lost ports to estimate it would require additional coherent access, not granted by retaining them. A sufficient microscopic consumer uses two controlled-path Hamiltonians Hi(t) on the same finite dilation, with a common initial stock and ∫︁∥H0−H1∥∞dt/ħ≤b. Duhamel’s identity gives ∥v0−v1∥≤b, hence Re⟨v0, v1⟩≥1 −b2/2. It requires a bound on the actual full dilation difference; equal averaged decay rates do not establish it. Sharpness below is for the declared Gram class, not for every Hamiltonian norm ball. The common conversion and uniform loss model can supply ηL when its own hypotheses still hold. Otherwise ηL needs a new certificate.
